title: Notification System
summary: Send push, email and SMS reliably at scale: an API that accepts events, user preferences and templates, per-channel queues and workers, provider failover, dedup, and delivery tracking.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Services trigger notifications to users over push (APNs/FCM), email, SMS, in-app
Respect user preferences, quiet hours and unsubscribes
Templates with localisation; scheduled and bulk sends
At-least-once delivery attempts, no duplicate sends to the user
Transactional (OTP) within seconds; marketing can lag

blocks.text: Ask early: are transactional and marketing traffic separate? (They must not share a queue — a 50M-user campaign shouldn't delay password resets.)
Throughput is dominated by bulk sends; latency requirements by transactional ones.

POST /v1/notifications
{
  "idempotency_key": "order-123-shipped",
  "user_ids": ["u1"],                 // or a segment id for bulk
  "template": "order_shipped",
  "data": {"order_id": "123"},
  "channels": ["push", "email"],      // optional; else preference-driven
  "priority": "transactional",
  "send_at": null
}
-> 202 {notification_id}

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: The idempotency key makes retries from upstream services safe: the same key within the dedup window returns the original notification id instead of sending again.

blocks.caption: Accept fast, deliver asynchronously per channel

items: API writes the request and returns 202; the orchestrator expands segments, applies preferences/quiet hours, renders templates.
Per-channel (and per-priority) queues isolate failures and let each channel scale independently.
Workers call providers, record status, and retry with backoff; provider callbacks (delivered, bounced) update the log.
At-least-once queues + **idempotent workers**: before sending, check (notification_id, channel, user) in a dedup store with a TTL.
Retries with exponential backoff and jitter; after N failures → dead-letter queue for inspection.
**Provider failover:** keep two providers per channel; a circuit breaker trips to the secondary when error rates spike.
Invalid push tokens (410 from APNs) must delete the token, or you'll keep paying to fail.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Calling email/SMS providers synchronously from the API request. One slow provider then backs up every product service that sends notifications.

sections.title: Deep dive: bulk sends and rate limits

items.title: Segment expansion
items.text: A campaign to 50M users is split into batches of ~1k users and enqueued gradually.

items.title: Throttling
items.text: Token buckets per provider (and per destination domain for email) keep you under provider quotas and sender reputation limits.

items.title: Per-user caps
items.text: Limit notifications per user per day; collapse duplicates ("3 new messages").

items.title: Scheduling
items.text: Store send_at; a scheduler moves due jobs to the queue; time-zone-aware sends are bucketed by zone.

items: Separate queues and worker pools for transactional vs bulk — the noisy-neighbour problem is the classic failure.
Shard the delivery log by notification id; keep it in a write-optimised store (Cassandra/Dynamo) with TTL.
In-app notifications are just rows in an inbox table plus a realtime push over the app's WebSocket.
Monitor per-channel success rate, latency and cost; alert on provider degradation.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Accept the request fast with an idempotency key, then deliver asynchronously through per-channel, per-priority queues with idempotent workers and provider failover.

items.q: How do you guarantee no duplicate SMS?
items.a: You can't guarantee exactly-once with an external provider, but dedup keys before send plus provider-side idempotency (where supported) make duplicates rare.

items.q: How do you handle quiet hours across time zones?
items.a: Store user time zone; if now is inside quiet hours, set send_at to the end of the window (unless priority is critical).
Tracking pixel and redirect links for email; app analytics events for push.

items.q: What if the preference service is down?
items.a: Fail closed for marketing (don't send), fail open with cached preferences for transactional.

items: Idempotent workers, backoff, DLQ, provider circuit breakers.
Token buckets per provider; per-user caps.
